name: Respiratory variants & flu
value: US flu admissions 9,584 (to 7 Nov); severity low
summary: Flu seasons start early in the US and England; US admissions rising, CDC rates severity low
state: CDC reported 9,584 flu hospital admissions in the week to 7 Nov, up on the previous week and mostly A(H1N1), while rating severity low for all ages; its forecast pointed to further rises to 28 Nov (CDC). UKHSA's report of 26 Nov, covering 16–22 Nov, shows flu at moderate levels and rising in England (UKHSA). Searches on 27 Nov found no new WHO variant designation and no health systems reported as strained, so Watch holds.
for_you: Older people, pregnant women and people with long-term conditions are most at risk from an early flu season. The NHS advises eligible people to get their flu and COVID-19 vaccines.
rubric_hit: Watch: unusually early northern-hemisphere flu season; US admissions 9,584 in week to 7 Nov (CDC)

why: Known viruses change; a new COVID-19 variant or a severe flu strain can strain health systems without being 'novel'.
drivers: Viral evolution, waning immunity, seasonal patterns, vaccine match.

rubric.alert: WHO designates a variant of concern, or flu or COVID-19 hospitalisations strain several countries' health systems.
rubric.watch: WHO designates a new variant of interest, or a hemisphere's flu season is unusually early or severe.
rubric.normal: No WHO variant of interest rising fast; flu seasons of normal severity.
